neighbours.label: the word for a hindrance or defect in a phrase about a limited ability or its absence ("ability to over|take", "w|obble-free")
fire: Heavy fog on the pass limits a driver's ability to overtake slower lorries.
The reinforced legs give the workbench a sturdy, wobble-free stance.
A speed governor reduces the ability to overtake on short straights.
Tighten each bolt firmly to get a wobble-free shelf.
Towing a caravan affects your ability to overtake and to brake.
The wide base keeps the tripod wobble-free even in wind.
Narrow lanes restrict the ability to overtake cyclists safely.
Add felt pads under the feet for a wobble-free chair.
quiet: Heavy fog on the pass limits a driver's ability to see slower lorries.
The reinforced legs give the workbench a sturdy, solid stance.
A speed governor reduces the top speed on short straights.
Tighten each bolt firmly to get a level shelf.
Towing a caravan affects your ability to steer and to brake.
The wide base keeps the tripod steady even in wind.
Narrow lanes restrict the space left for cyclists.
Add felt pads under the feet to protect the floor.

notes: Low confidence. Top examples: over(take), decay(ed), backlash, traumatic, weight, wobble(-free), injury (prevention), blight(-resistant). Probes: 'ability to overtake' 0.45, 'wobble-free' 0.37, but 'tried to overtake' 0.12, 'blight-resistant' 0.09, 'injury prevention' 0.01, 'no longer dangerous' 0.01. The test uses only the two shapes that fired, so a hold would support those two phrases, not the wider guess.
